item.title: EPA Proposes to Relax Air Pollution Standards for Buses, Trucks
item.description: The US Environmental Protection Agency on Thursday proposed rolling back emission standards for new heavy-duty trucks, including buses, garbage trucks and semis.

item.title: Microsoft’s Emissions Surged 25% in 2025 During Data Center Boom
item.description: Microsoft Corp. said its carbon emissions climbed 25% in 2025, making it the latest technology company to report a setback in its efforts to erase emissions amid heavy spending on artificial intelligence data centers.

item.title: How a Heat Wave Pushed the UK’s Power Grid to Its Limit
item.description: On a sweltering day in late June, the UK’s power grid came under exceptional strain. As temperatures rose, wind generation slumped and electricity prices spiked, forcing Britain’s grid operator to take emergency measures to keep the lights on.

item.title: El Niño Likely Strongest in 75 Years, US Forecasters Say
item.description: The weather-roiling El Niño that emerged across the Pacific last month has continued to build and will likely be one of the strongest in more than 75 years, the US Climate Prediction Center said.

item.title: Suppliers to Top Fashion Brands Face a Rising Climate Challenge
item.description: Manufacturers have a difficult, and costly, task to adapt production lines and protect workers.

item.title: China Climate Plan Pushes Renewables in Factories, Data Centers
item.description: China, the world’s largest source of climate-warming greenhouse gases, plans to more deeply integrate its massive renewable power fleet into factories, data centers and transport in a new plan that lays out more detail of its emissions-cutting strategy through 2030.

item.title: How Trump and AI Data Centers Are Boosting Nuclear Power
item.description: Nuclear energy is back in vogue in the US.

item.title: Europe’s Expanding Heat Wave Tests Power Grids and Fire Defenses
item.description: Europe’s third major heat wave this year is set to intensify and expand, extending from west to east over the coming week.

item.title: EU Plans 2040 Electrification Target to Cut Oil, Gas Consumption
item.description: The European Union wants to propose an electrification goal for the next decade as part of a plan to strengthen the local market for clean technologies and help shift the bloc away from fossil fuels.

item.title: Hundreds of Snakes on the Loose After Severe Flooding in China
item.description: The heavy flooding in China’s Guangxi region has created an unusual secondary hazard: hundreds of snakes escaping from inundated breeding farms.

item.title: Super El Niño Will Give Us a Glimpse of Life in 2035
item.description: Over the next year, the naturally occurring El Niño weather pattern will add to growing damage from climate change.

item.title: China’s Top Solar Firm Makes Switch From Silver to Copper
item.description: China’s biggest solar maker has begun producing cells that replace silver with copper, in response to soaring prices of the precious metal that have rattled the industry since last year.

item.title: ‘Gargantuan’ Typhoon Threatens More Floods in Rain-Soaked China
item.description: China is facing more torrential rain and flooding this weekend from a massive typhoon tracking toward the country’s east coast, following recent severe storms that led to deaths and crop damage.

item.title: Top Fashion Brands Have a Supply Chain Battle Against Extreme Heat
item.description: The global garment industry is beginning to address impacts of record temperatures, which threaten tens of millions of workers and erode productivity.

item.title: UK Issues Electricity Supply Warning as Heat Wave Strains Grid
item.description: The UK grid operator issued a rare summer warning, citing tight electricity supplies as a blistering heat wave strains energy systems across Europe.

item.title: UK, EDF Reach Deal to Extend Life of Sizewell B Nuclear Plant
item.description: The UK government reached a draft deal with Electricite de France SA to extend the life of a key nuclear plant beyond the middle of the century, as the nation seeks to cut reliance on fossil fuels for power generation.

item.title: California Chosen for Peak Energy’s Sodium-Ion Battery Plant
item.description: Peak Energy said it’s building what it describes as the first commercial US manufacturing facility for grid-scale sodium-ion energy storage systems in Sacramento, California.

item.title: How Climate Change Could Raise Your Water Bill
item.description: Extreme weather is already fueling higher insurance premiums and grocery prices. A new study based on Santa Cruz, California suggests water rates are also at risk.

item.title: Meat Giant JBS Pulls Back From 2040 Net-Zero Emissions Goal
item.description: JBS NV, the world’s largest meatpacker, is stepping back from a 2040 net-zero emissions goal, dropping targets for the indirect emissions that make up the bulk of its environmental footprint.

item.title: Private Equity Funds Seek Climate Experts as Risks Rise
item.description: Investors are turning to specialist tools and companies to understand escalating threats from extreme weather events.

item.title: Wildfire Risk Rises Across US West as Winds, Dry Lightning Build
item.description: Strong winds and dry thunderstorms are raising the risk of fast-moving wildfires across much of the US West, where forecasters warned conditions will favor new ignitions and rapid fire spread through Thursday.

item.title: EU Plans More Flexibility for Industry in Carbon Overhaul
item.description: The European Union aims to give its ailing industrial sector more flexibility in an upcoming reform of the bloc’s flagship carbon market, while ensuring companies boost investment in clean technologies.

item.title: Heat Wave Threatens Output at Five French Nuclear Reactors
item.description: France’s latest heat wave is straining the country’s power system, with Electricite de France SA warning that as many as five nuclear plants could face output curbs in the coming days as soaring temperatures affect rivers used for cooling.

item.title: London Wants a Much Bigger Chunk of the Catastrophe Bond Market
item.description: The world’s biggest hub for commercial and specialty risk is angling for a much more prominent role in the $140 billion global market for insurance-linked securities.

item.title: Nuclear Power to Climb 44% Worldwide as China Tops US, BNEF Says
item.description: Global nuclear capacity is set to climb 44% over the next decade after years of tepid growth, spurred by growing demand for electricity and aggressive efforts to build reactors in China and India.

item.title: Milan’s Battle Against Bad Air Goes On
item.description: A quirk of geography has hampered the Italian city’s ongoing efforts to reduce pollution from vehicle emissions and other regional sources.

item.title: Tencent Inks First Deal for Carbon-Removal Credits Outside China
item.description: Tencent Holdings Ltd will buy 300,000 carbon removal credits from an agroforestry project in Indonesia, marking the first deal of its kind for the Chinese technology firm outside its domestic market.

item.title: China’s Deadly Storms Turbocharged by Convergence of Factors
item.description: This week’s deadly storms in southern and central China were worsened by a convergence of factors, underscoring the growing frequency of weather extremes that the world’s second-largest economy must increasingly contend with.

item.title: Coffee Trader Seeks to Shield More Vietnam Growers From Weather
item.description: Major coffee trader ECOM Agroindustrial Corp. is pushing for a fivefold increase in the number of growers covered by its specialty weather insurance in Vietnam, where the industry depends on thousands of smallholder farmers increasingly exposed to climate risk.

item.title: Private Equity Plays Heat Detective as Climate Analytics Boom
item.description: For decades, investment models at the largest private equity funds relied on assumptions of relatively stable weather patterns. Now frequent extreme events are creating new threats for their portfolio companies.
